title: Kundl Gorge Kundler Klamm
name: Kundl Gorge Kundler Klamm
kurzbeschreibung: The Kundler Klamm: a family-friendly natural gorge between Kundl and the Wildschönau featuring the roaring Wildschönauer Ache and a slow train.
beschreibung:
Overview

The imposing Kundler Klamm connects the Tyrolean market town of Kundl in the Unterinntal with the idyllic high valley of the Wildschönau in the Kufstein district. Flanked by soaring limestone cliffs, the wide canyon trail winds along the foaming Wildschönauer Ache at an altitude of around 530 to 650 metres. As one of the few gorges in Tyrol that runs almost completely level without steep staircases, the Kundler Klamm is an exceptionally popular and low-barrier excursion destination for families with children and seniors.

Geology & Family Experience

The formation of the gorge dates back to the last ice age, when melting glacial waters carved deeply into the limestone and dolomite rocks. According to local legend, however, the gorge owes its existence to a dragon that once dwelt in the high valley; in its death throes, it bit through the rock, allowing the trapped lake to drain and the valley to be settled. Today, the roughly 2.9-kilometre-long, well-paved walking trail enchants visitors with bizarre rock formations, covered wooden galleries, and shady riverside resting areas. Geologically interested visitors can discover colorful pebbles and fossils along the riverbed; at the Kundler Steindreherei stone-turning workshop at the gorge entrance, these stones are crafted into artistic souvenirs. A special highlight for families is the colorful slow train Bummelzug Wildschönau, which ambles leisurely between Mühltal and the gorge entrance during the summer season.

Visit & Getting There

The Kundler Klamm is freely accessible and free of charge daily from early May to late October (the gorge may be closed at short notice during severe storms or flooding; winter closure is enforced in winter due to rockfall hazard). Trips on the slow train are subject to a fee (adult single ticket approx. €6.00, children approx. €3.50). Getting there by car from the Inntal side: via the A12 Inntalautobahn (exit Wörgl West or Kramsach), follow the B171 to Kundl and follow signs to the Kundler Klamm (large car park in front of the gorge bridge). By public transport: ÖBB train to Kundl railway station, from there approx. 20 minutes on foot or via Regiobus to the gorge entrance.

Tips

The path through the Kundler Klamm is wide, well gravelled, and easily passable with all-terrain strollers. On warm summer days, shallow gravel banks along the riverbank offer delightful spots for skimming stones and wading in the refreshing mountain water. At the entrance to the valley in Kundl, the traditional Gasthof Kundler Klamm invites guests to enjoy hearty Tyrolean specialties in its shady beer garden.
